hypotheses.explanation: edit_surface mutates the existing shared material: material = original performs no copy. Copying the target mesh preserves references to its materials. The compiler caches materials by finish, explaining propagation to the four supports, backrest, and storage mesh.

camera_calibration.reason: set_view directly assigns the requested sensor width; only floating-point error is expected.

geometry_replay.reason: Emission multiplies the primitive world matrix by geometry_frame, including nonuniform scale. No geometry defect is evident.

position_replay.reason: The emitted world transform includes geometry_frame and primitive origin; the existing group translation matches offset plus final_move.

visibility_isolation.reason: All six furniture meshes exist, and the visibility function recursively sets hide_render on descendants.

support_relation.reason: The function corrects the measured world-space bottom against the surface top. Expect a near-zero residual with Floor.001 as the surface, allowing approximate AABB and evaluation effects.

dependency_move.reason: All six furniture meshes have their named part markers under StudyBench; their transforms should follow the group.

material_dependency.reason: Expect six non-target changes, matching the supplied direct comparison. The interval allows uncertainty about runtime ownership; shared material identities are not included in the snapshot.

hypotheses.explanation: An alternative responsibility boundary is that prepare_edit_mesh should establish exclusive ownership of all editable data, including materials. It copies only the mesh datablock, leaving shared shader references. This explains the same leakage, although edit_surface is the more direct repair location.

camera_calibration.reason: Material ownership does not affect direct sensor assignment; this probe does not distinguish H1 and H2.

geometry_replay.reason: Both explanations leave geometry-frame multiplication intact and predict the same small numerical residual.

position_replay.reason: Both explanations leave primitive origins and group movement intact.

visibility_isolation.reason: Recursive visibility operates independently of mesh/material ownership; the same near-zero outcome is expected.

support_relation.reason: With Floor.001 as the surface, world-space AABB correction should work under either explanation.

dependency_move.reason: Copying mesh data does not change the observed named-part hierarchy; both hypotheses predict proper following.

material_dependency.reason: The same six shared-material users should change. This outcome cannot distinguish whether isolation belongs in preparation or surface editing.
